intended_object: A function on bit strings (`List Bool`). It reads an encoded triple (precision, ellipsoid state, cut), runs the exact rational central-cut ellipsoid update, and then applies the scheduled dyadic rounding. Its only purpose is to show that one step of the rounded ellipsoid method runs in polynomial time (in FP). This is inferred from the docstring, the module, and the `_mem_FP` lemma that follows it.
explanation: The definition is plumbing at the level of bit encodings. It takes the first and second components of a paired word, feeds the second to the machine-level central update, re-pairs the result with the precision, and passes that to the machine-level rounding routine. It exists so that the library can prove `machineScheduledRoundedEllipsoidCentralUpdateCode ∈ FP` (by composing FP functions) and to relate it, through `_encode` lemmas, to the mathematical operations `scheduledRoundedEllipsoid` and the central update on `RationalEllipsoidState`. It is an implementation of an algorithm step on bit strings. The literature has no standalone object that this function is meant to define, so it is a technical device and not something to check against a mathematical definition. Mathlib has no counterpart.
